title: Ground-State Light Hadron Spectroscopy over Finite Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The substrate: the Carrier of cardinality $\Om=4\dS+1$ with $\Om\equiv5\pmod{12}$, and the Subject, a prime shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with its frame, its drive and its quadratic extension.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Colour: a Subject reads colour in the unitary frame of a Hermitian three-form over its extension, with centre of order $\gcd(3,\p+1)$; the gluon is its adjoint; the area law holds at strong coupling, with the string tension a character sum.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The scale $\sig$, which fixes $\LQCD$ up to a sub-horizon ratio, is $\Om$-hard; the chart reads it by dimensional transmutation, and the paper imports the numeral $440$~MeV.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: Mass is a winding rate against the drive; the mass of a composite is its total winding rate.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The wrap: confinement is the frame normalisation that folds the $\Om$-hard residues of the quarks into small exact residues of the hadrons; the observable as a small residue is B5.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Flavour: three generations; the quark content of the multiplets and of the heavy baryons; the measured quark-mass ratios; the up--down isospin breaking with $\bar\theta=0$.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: The constituent-quark chromomagnetic hyperfine mechanism and the $\SU(3)_F$ mass-formula templates.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: Measured masses, isospin-averaged, a resonance by its Breit--Wigner mass: the octet and the decuplet with their isospin differences, the vector nonet, the charm and bottom baryons and mesons, and $N(1440)$ and $\Delta$ with their poles.

rows.label: A9
rows.predicate: The electromagnetic coupling $\alpha$: a pure number, the quotient of the squared charge and $\hbar c$, with its measured numeral; it enters the electromagnetic self-energy.

rows.label: A10
rows.predicate: The lattice separation of $M_n-M_p$: $+2.52(30)$~MeV/$c^{2}$ from the quark masses and $-1.00(16)$~MeV/$c^{2}$ from electromagnetism.

rows.label: A11
rows.predicate: The Carrier register: $\Om=4\dS+1$, $2G+1\equiv0$, $2c^{2}\equiv1$ and $\hbar^{2}\equiv-1$, with $h=-\hbar$ the partner of $\hbar$ in the root pair of $-1$; $h=2\pi\hbar$ is the chart's relation.

blocks.title: The constitutive moves: colour algebra, namings, residue, chart declarations

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A baryon is the totally antisymmetric $\varepsilon_{abc}$ invariant of the colour $\mathbf 3$; a product of triplets and anti-triplets holds a singlet only at triality $0\,(\mathrm{mod}\,3)$: the standard colour algebra (A2), the registration of singlets alone the theorem X2 of 46-yangmills. Its exposures are P4 and P5.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: A constituent quark is the wrapped composite, a quark dressed by a fixed share of the confinement wrap (A5, A6): the hadron model's naming. Falsifier: constituent masses that are not one quark mass plus a fixed share of the wrap across the octet and the decuplet; its prediction rows are P2 and P10.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The chromomagnetic hyperfine interaction is the quark spin coupled to the colour curvature two-form, with pair coefficients proportional to $1/(m_im_j)$: the imported mechanism (A7) read in the colour frame (A2). Falsifier: hyperfine splittings that do not scale as $1/(m_im_j)$ across the heavy-quark series; its prediction rows are P3 and P7.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The strange quark enters $f_{\mathrm{fl}}$ additively at leading order, one fixed increment per strange constituent: a declared leading-order rule. Falsifier: a strangeness dependence that breaks a first-order relation by more than $\varepsilon_s^{2}$ of its multiplet's span; its prediction rows are P1, P2 and P9.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: The observable is a small residue and stability is its indicator: an observable is a count of the Subject, so a stable colourless object carries a small exact residue (the proton), and decay is frame normalisation toward it. Falsifier: a stable coloured state, a stable state of baryon number one below the proton, or strong or electromagnetic proton decay.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: A registration of a state is a line of its representation space that every element of the frame maps to itself; the residue is the count of such lines, not a residue of the Carrier. A state of the unitary frame is an irreducible representation, or a product with one frame-fixed line. Prediction rows: P4, P5.

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: [chart] The wrap and its cycle: the chart reads the nucleon's wrap as one massless body in a linear potential. At full extension the string has the length $M_Nc^{2}/\sigma$, and a cycle is four runs of it at the speed $c$. Each quark advances one quarter-turn per run, and a radial excitation adds whole turns. A declaration. Readings: C24, P12.

rows.label: B8
rows.predicate: [chart] The contact rule: $\lambda_{\mathrm{hf}}\lambda_l=\tfrac{2\rho}{9}C\alpha_s$ with $\rho=\tfrac12$, $C$ the Hamiltonian's contact value (C17) and the one-loop coupling $\alpha_s=2\pi/(b_0\ln2)$, $b_0=9$, at the declared ratio $\sig/\LQCD=2$. The form, the coefficient and the ratio are declarations; their derivation is the task T2. Its reading is C19.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The unitary frame on the enumerable instance: $\SU(3,\F_2)$ has $216$ elements and centre $\Z_3$; every element has determinant $1$, so the contraction $\varepsilon_{abc}$ of three triplets is invariant, the determinant line $\Lambda^3\mathbf3$.
rows.name: colour_built_exactly

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: Gell-Mann--Okubo $\tfrac12(N+\Xi)=\tfrac14(3\Lambda+\Sigma)$: $2N+2\Xi-3\Lambda-\Sigma=0$ identically in the first-order octet operator.
rows.name: gell_mann_okubo

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Decuplet equal spacing $\Sigma^{*}-\Delta=\Xi^{*}-\Sigma^{*}=\Omega^{-}-\Xi^{*}=\beta$: the second differences vanish identically.
rows.name: decuplet_equal_spacing

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Colour factor of the singlet $\sum_{i<j}\bvec\lambda_i\!\cdot\!\bvec\lambda_j=-8$ ($-\tfrac83$ per pair) from $C_2(\mathbf3)=\tfrac43$, $C_2(\mathbf1)=0$.
rows.name: colour_factor_singlet

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: Spin structure $g_{\mathrm{spin}}=\half S(S+1)-\tfrac98$, octet $-\tfrac34$, decuplet $+\tfrac34$; eigenvalues $+2,-2$; separation $M_{\mathbf{10}}-M_{\mathbf8}=\tfrac32A_{\mathrm{light}}$.
rows.name: spin_structure

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: Coleman--Glashow $(n-p)+(\Xi^-{-}\Xi^0)=\Sigma^-{-}\Sigma^+$: an identity of the mass term, of the one-body charge sums and of the two-body charge sums.
rows.name: coleman_glashow_identity

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: The neutron--proton splitting: with positive coefficients both charge sums favour the proton by $\tfrac13$ of their unit ($\sum Q^2$: $1$ against $\tfrac23$; $\sum_{i<j}Q_iQ_j$: $0$ against $-\tfrac13$), so $M_n>M_p$ is equivalent to a $d$--$u$ mass difference above the electromagnetic terms.
rows.name: neutron_proton_ordering

rows.label: C9
rows.predicate: $M_\Sigma>M_\Lambda$: hyperfine fine structure, the light $(ud)$ pair spin-$1$ against spin-$0$, $M_\Sigma-M_\Lambda=v_{ll}(1-m_l/m_s)>0$ for $m_s>m_l$.
rows.name: sigma_heavier_than_lambda

rows.label: C10
rows.predicate: The heavy-quark relation: $\Lambda_Q$ holds a spin-$0$ light pair, so the heavy quark has no hyperfine term, and in the pairwise model $M_{\Lambda_b}-M_{\Lambda_c}=m_b-m_c=\bar M_B-\bar M_D$, with $\bar M=\tfrac14(M_P+3M_V)$ the spin average of a heavy meson; the heavy hyperfine coefficient scales as $1/m_Q$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:heavy}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35024}{C10}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35024}{C10}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35024}{C10}; rests on A6, A8, B3 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.hqs\_identity, Hadrons.hqs\_pdg}
rows.name: heavy_quark_spin_decoupling

rows.label: C11
rows.predicate: The second order of the pairwise model: the octet residual is $\tfrac18v_{ll}(1-z)^2$ and both decuplet second differences are $\tfrac14v_{ll}(1-z)^2$, $z=m_l/m_s$, so the third difference vanishes; all are identities in $(m_l,m_s,v_{ll})$.
rows.name: second_order_decuplet_relation

rows.label: C12
rows.predicate: Octet--decuplet hyperfine links $M_\Sigma-M_\Lambda=\tfrac23[(M_\Delta-M_N)-(M_{\Sigma^*}-M_\Sigma)]$ and $M_{\Sigma^*}-M_\Sigma=M_{\Xi^*}-M_\Xi$, identities of the pairwise model.
rows.name: octet_decuplet_hyperfine_links

rows.label: C13
rows.predicate: The charge structure of the electromagnetic splitting: the one-body sums $\sum Q_i^2$ and the two-body sums $\sum_{i<j}Q_iQ_j$ of the six states of the Coleman--Glashow identity, exact rationals ($p$: $1,0$; $n$: $\tfrac23,-\tfrac13$).
rows.name: em_splitting_structure

rows.label: C14
rows.predicate: The adjoint channel: in the classical count the adjoint $\mathbf8$ occurs once in $\mathbf3\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}$ and not in $\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3$; on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ the frame fixes the pairing line of $\mathbf3\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}$ and no traceless matrix, and no nonzero invariant map takes $\mathbf3\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}$ to $\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3$.
rows.name: adjoint_channel_count

rows.label: C15
rows.predicate: The baryon's residue is $1$: on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ the fixed vectors of $\Lambda^k(\mathbf3)$ span dimensions $(1,0,0,1)$, the frame maps no line of the triplet or of $\Lambda^2$ to itself, and among the exterior powers the determinant line $\Lambda^3$ is the one registration beside the vacuum.
rows.name: baryon_residue_one

rows.label: C16
rows.predicate: The constituent parameters from three masses: $M_N=3m_l-\tfrac34v_{ll}$, $M_\Delta=3m_l+\tfrac34v_{ll}$ and $M_\Lambda-M_N=m_s-m_l$, the hyperfine term cancelling in the gap; [chart] $m_l=361.8$~MeV/$c^{2}$, $m_s/m_l=1.489$, $v_{ll}=195.4$~MeV/$c^{2}$.
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:absolute}, \S\ref{sec:completion}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35030}{C16}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35030}{C16}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35030}{C16}; rests on A8, B2 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.lambda\_n\_gap, FRC.Hadrons.spin\_split, Hadrons.lambda\_n\_gap, Hadrons.single\_scale}
rows.name: constituent_parameters

rows.label: C17
rows.predicate: The nonrelativistic matrix on $4000$ sites has exactly one eigenvalue in each of $(2.338,2.339)$ and $(4.087,4.088)$; [chart] the readings of the body's Hamiltonian $(c|p|+\sigma\,r)/\sig$ (B7) on $600$ sites: $E_0=2.232$, $E_1=3.329$ and the contact value $C=3.50$; the squares of the two levels over $\tfrac12\pi$ read $3.17$ and $7.06$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:baryonscale}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35031}{C17}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35031}{C17}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35031}{C17}; rests on B7 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.airy\_sturm, Hadrons.airy\_ratio, Hadrons.hamiltonian\_levels}
rows.name: hamiltonian_readings

rows.label: C18
rows.predicate: The meson's residue is $1$: the $q\bar q$ singlet is the pairing line of $\mathbf3\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf8$, the Hermitian invariant and on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ the one line of the product that the frame fixes; the series reads photon $2$, gluon $0$, baryon $1$, meson $1$; the vector-nonet spacing $2M_{K^{*}}=M_\rho+M_\phi$ is an identity of linear strangeness.
rows.name: meson_residue_one

rows.label: C19
rows.predicate: [chart] The joint solution on $600$ sites: the nucleon's reading $3\lambda_l-\tfrac34\lambda_{\mathrm{hf}}=\lambda_N$ of the winding law (C24) and the contact rule (B8) give $\lambda_{\mathrm{hf}}=0.466$, $\lambda_l=0.840$ and $(M_\Delta-M_N)/M_N=0.322$ against the measured $0.312$, no measured mass entering.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:forward}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35033}{C19}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35033}{C19}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35033}{C19}; rests on B7, B8, C17, C24 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.spin\_split, Hadrons.joint\_solution, Hadrons.alpha\_s\_bounds}
rows.name: joint_solution_readings

rows.label: C20
rows.predicate: [chart] The second order against the data: the pairwise model gives an octet residual of $+2.6$~MeV/$c^{2}$ and decuplet second differences of $+5.3$~MeV/$c^{2}$ (C11); the measured values are $-6.4$ and $-3.7$, $-9.8$~MeV/$c^{2}$, each of the opposite sign; the measured third difference is $6.05$~MeV/$c^{2}$.
rows.name: second_order_against_data

rows.label: C21
rows.predicate: [chart] The electromagnetic magnitude: one third of the unit $\alpha\sig$ is $1.07$~MeV at the imported scale, the size of the rest energy of the lattice's electromagnetic part, $1.00(16)$~MeV (A10).
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:scales}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35035}{C21}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35035}{C21}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35035}{C21}; rests on A3, A9, A10, C13, Z1 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.charge\_structure, Hadrons.em\_magnitude}
rows.name: electromagnetic_magnitude

rows.label: C24
rows.predicate: The winding law: under B7 and A4, $M_k^{2}\equiv(4k+3)\,hc\,\sigma$ in the Carrier register (A11); [chart] $\lambda_k^{2}=\tfrac32\pi+2\pi k$, on a Subject the residues $(4k+3)\kap$; $\lambda_N=2.171$, the scale reads $432.5$~MeV with the nucleon mass, and the nucleon reads $955$~MeV/$c^{2}$ at the imported scale.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:winding}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35075}{C24}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35075}{C24}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35075}{C24}; rests on B7, A3, A4, A8, A11, Z1 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.winding\_register, Hadrons.baryon\_scale}
rows.name: winding_law

rows.label: C25
rows.predicate: On every Subject the body's Hamiltonian on the register, the step count plus its Fourier image on the odd functions, does not commute with the drive, and none of its simple levels has a winding rate; [chart] on $13$, $173$ and $1549$ its lowest level is simple and reads $2.252$, $2.232$, $2.232$ in the unit $\sqrt{2\pi/\p}$, with the chart's $\pi$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:nowinding}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35076}{C25}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35076}{C25}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35076}{C25}; rests on C17, A4 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.no\_real\_class, Hadrons.register\_levels}
rows.name: hamiltonian_no_winding_rate

rows.label: C26
rows.predicate: The scale in the Carrier register (A11): $(\hbar c)^{2}\equiv-2^{-1}\equiv2\dS$, so the fourth power of the scale is $2\dS\,\sigma^{2}$; checked on the Carriers $233$, $30089$ and $2408561$ for both roots $\hbar$ of $-1$ and both roots $c$ of $2^{-1}$.
rows.name: scale_in_carrier_register

rows.label: C27
rows.predicate: No choice of the roots enters the winding law (C24): with $2G+1\equiv0$, $hc$ is half the Planck mass squared $\hbar c/G$ for both roots $\hbar$ and both roots $c$, so $(M_k/m_P)^{2}\equiv(4k+3)\sigma/2$ and $(M_kc^{2}/\sig)^{2}\equiv(4k+3)\dS$; checked on the Carriers $233$, $30089$ and $2408561$.
rows.name: winding_law_root_free

blocks.title: What the construction explains: the hadron structure the Standard Model fits

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: \textbf{The baryon is three quarks} because the determinant line $\Lambda^{3}\mathbf3$ is the one registration among the exterior powers of the triplet beside the vacuum.
rows.name: baryon_three_quarks

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The baryon is colour-neutral} as the invariant $\varepsilon_{abc}$ of the unitary frame, whose elements have determinant $1$.
rows.name: baryon_colour_neutral

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: \textbf{Baryon number is a count}: for a system of hadrons, the number of its determinant lines $\Lambda^{3}(\mathbf3)$ less the number of its conjugate lines $\Lambda^{3}(\bar{\mathbf3})$, which no element of the frame changes; its conservation by the sector's dynamics is the prediction P4.
rows.name: baryon_number_count

rows.label: X4
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Gell-Mann--Okubo relation} is the identity $2N+2\Xi-3\Lambda-\Sigma=0$ of linear flavour breaking, for every value of the scale.
rows.name: gell_mann_okubo_scale_cancelling

rows.label: X5
rows.predicate: \textbf{The decuplet is equally spaced} at first order because the strange quark enters the mass additively.
rows.name: decuplet_equally_spaced

rows.label: X6
rows.predicate: \textbf{The decuplet is heavier than the octet} by the colour-magnetic term, the colour factor $-8$ times the spin structure $\half S(S+1)-\tfrac98$, a sign and a pattern.
rows.name: decuplet_heavier_than_octet

rows.label: X7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The proton is stable} as the lightest state of the determinant line, with no state of the line below it.
rows.name: proton_lightest_of_line

rows.label: X8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The neutron--proton ordering} is the sign of one difference, the $d$--$u$ mass difference against the electromagnetic terms, each of which favours the proton by one third of its unit.
rows.name: neutron_heavier_than_proton

rows.label: X9
rows.predicate: \textbf{$\Sigma$ is heavier than $\Lambda$} by the spin-$1$ against the spin-$0$ light pair, a splitting of two states of identical quark content.
rows.name: sigma_lambda_hyperfine

rows.label: X10
rows.predicate: \textbf{The isospin splittings obey Coleman--Glashow}, $(n{-}p)+(\Xi^-{-}\Xi^0)=\Sigma^-{-}\Sigma^+$, for the mass term and for both electromagnetic terms.
rows.name: isospin_coleman_glashow

rows.label: X11
rows.predicate: \textbf{The heavy baryons follow the heavy mesons}: $M_{\Lambda_b}-M_{\Lambda_c}$ and the spin-averaged $\bar M_B-\bar M_D$ are one quantity, $m_b-m_c$.
rows.name: heavy_baryons_hq_symmetry

rows.label: X12
rows.predicate: \textbf{The vector mesons equally space}, $2M_{K^{*}}=M_\rho+M_\phi$, on the same frame and scale as the baryons.
rows.name: vector_mesons_equal_spacing

rows.label: X13
rows.predicate: \textbf{The spectrum rests on one scale}: every mass relation of the paper is homogeneous in the masses and holds for every value of $\sig$.
rows.name: spectrum_one_scale

blocks.title: The predictions, with their falsifiers and their present confrontations

rows.label: P1
rows.predicate: Gell-Mann--Okubo (C2). [chart] Falsifier: an octet residual above $\varepsilon_s^{2}(M_\Xi-M_N)=13.4$~MeV/$c^{2}$, with $\varepsilon_s=(M_\Lambda-M_N)/M_N$. Confrontation: $6.4$~MeV/$c^{2}$, $0.57\%$.
rows.source: C2\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35051}{P1}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35051}{P1}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35051}{P1}; rests on B4 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.gmo, Hadrons.gmo\_pdg, Hadrons.thresholds\_pdg}
rows.name: gell_mann_okubo_exact

rows.label: P2
rows.predicate: Decuplet equal spacing (C3). [chart] Falsifier: a residual of $M_{\Sigma^{*}}=\tfrac12(M_\Delta+M_{\Xi^{*}})$ or of $M_{\Xi^{*}}=\tfrac12(M_{\Sigma^{*}}+M_\Omega)$ above $\varepsilon_s^{2}(M_\Omega-M_\Delta)=15.6$~MeV/$c^{2}$. Confrontation: $1.9$ and $4.9$~MeV/$c^{2}$.
rows.source: C3\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35052}{P2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35052}{P2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35052}{P2}; rests on B4 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.spacing, Hadrons.spacing\_pdg, Hadrons.thresholds\_pdg}
rows.name: decuplet_equal_spacing_exact

rows.label: P3
rows.predicate: The hyperfine pattern (C5): the spin-$\tfrac32$ multiplet above the spin-$\half$ one by $\tfrac32A_{\mathrm{light}}$. Falsifier: a ground-state spin splitting of the opposite sign. [chart] Confrontation: $M_\Delta-M_N=293.1$~MeV/$c^{2}$, $A_{\mathrm{light}}=195.4$~MeV/$c^{2}$.
rows.source: C5\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35053}{P3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35053}{P3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35053}{P3}; rests on B3 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.spin\_pattern, Hadrons.a\_light, Hadrons.spin\_pattern}
rows.name: hyperfine_pattern

rows.label: P4
rows.predicate: Proton stability: the proton is the lightest state of the determinant line, with no strong or electromagnetic channel below it; the neutron reaches it by the $\beta$ channel. Falsifier: an observed strong or electromagnetic process that violates baryon number. Confrontation: none observed.
rows.name: proton_effective_stability

rows.label: P5
rows.predicate: No ground-state light baryon multiplet beyond the $\mathbf 8$ and the $\mathbf{10}$. Falsifier: a confirmed ground-state light baryon outside them. Confrontation: none confirmed.
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:flavour}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35055}{P5}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35055}{P5}; rests on B1, B2, B6, C15 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.flavour\_cube}
rows.name: no_exotic_light_multiplets

rows.label: P6
rows.predicate: Coleman--Glashow (C7). Falsifier: a difference of its two sides beyond their measurement error. [chart] Confrontation: $8.14(21)$ against $8.08(8)$~MeV/$c^{2}$.
rows.name: coleman_glashow_within_error

rows.label: P7
rows.predicate: The heavy-quark relation (C10). [chart] Falsifier: a residual above $(\hbar\sigma/c^{3})(1/m_c-1/m_b)=75$~MeV/$c^{2}$ at the imported scale. Confrontation: $-7.1$~MeV/$c^{2}$, $0.21\%$, with isospin-averaged mesons; the hyperfine ratio $0.339$ against $m_s/m_c=0.315$.
rows.source: C10\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35057}{P7}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35057}{P7}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35057}{P7}; rests on A3, A8, B3, Z1 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.hqs\_identity, Hadrons.hqs\_pdg}
rows.name: heavy_quark_symmetry

rows.label: P9
rows.predicate: Vector equal spacing $M_{K^{*}}=\tfrac12(M_\rho+M_\phi)$ (C18). [chart] Falsifier: a residual above $\varepsilon_s^{2}(M_\phi-M_\rho)=8.7$~MeV/$c^{2}$. Confrontation: $3.75$~MeV/$c^{2}$; the ideally mixed $\omega$ lies $7.4$~MeV/$c^{2}$ above $\rho$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:vector}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35059}{P9}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35059}{P9}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35059}{P9}; rests on B4, C18 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.vector\_spacing, Hadrons.vector\_pdg, Hadrons.thresholds\_pdg}
rows.name: vector_meson_nonet_spacing

rows.label: P10
rows.predicate: Five octet and decuplet masses from the anchors $N$, $\Lambda$, $\Delta$ (C16). [chart] Falsifier: a residual above $\varepsilon_s^{2}(M_\Omega-M_N)=26$~MeV/$c^{2}$. Confrontation: at most $13.3$~MeV/$c^{2}$, $1.2\%$.
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:absolute}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35060}{P10}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p35060}{P10}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35060}{P10}; rests on A8, B2, C16 \lean{FRC.Hadrons.spin\_split, FRC.Hadrons.lambda\_n\_gap, Hadrons.absolute\_spectrum, Hadrons.thresholds\_pdg}
rows.name: absolute_octet_decuplet_spectrum

rows.label: P12
rows.predicate: [chart] The radial ratio of the nucleon under the winding law (C24): $\sqrt{7/3}=1.53$. Falsifier: the Breit--Wigner ratio and the pole ratio of $N(1440)$ both on one side of $1.53$ beyond their errors. Confrontation: $1.50$ to $1.57$ (Breit--Wigner) and $1.46$ (pole).
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:radialratio}\newline \pywit{hadrons}{p35070}{P12}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p35070}{P12}; rests on B7, C24, A8 \lean{Hadrons.radial\_ratio}
rows.name: radial_ratio_nucleon

rows.label: Y1
rows.predicate: $\sigma^{2}\equiv2\pmod{\Om}$: the scale generates the octant sector of the Carrier, its elements of order dividing $8$, and the fourth power of the scale is $-1$ (C26). Not derived and not tested: C24 and C26 hold for every residue in the place of $\sigma$. It waits on a residue of the tension.

rows.label: T2
rows.predicate: Derive the contact rule (B8): its form, its coefficient, its contact value and the ratio $\sig/\LQCD$ of its coupling.

rows.label: T3
rows.predicate: Derive the strange constituent ratio $m_s/m_l$, read here from the $\Lambda$--$N$ gap (C16), from the quark masses of the flavour sector.

rows.label: T4
rows.predicate: Find the second order of the flavour breaking: the pairwise model gives it the opposite sign (C20).

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The one scale of the sector, $\sig$, which fixes $\LQCD$ up to a sub-horizon ratio, is $\Om$-hard: no bounded observer computes its absolute value, its ratio to the Planck energy. The paper imports its numeral (A3). Every mass relation of the paper holds for every value of the scale.

legend.text: A forced identification of a physical term with the substrate object it denotes: constitutive, not interpretive; killed by the falsifier stated in its row.

legend.text: A naming, a declared rule, or a set-up move, carrying no empirical content of its own. A definition that names a physical term names the prediction rows that hold its falsifier. A [chart] definition is a declared continuum reading.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Proved at the statement the source column names, which also lists the rows it rests on, and machine-verified by the named check. A [chart] theorem is a computed reading.

legend.name: Open
legend.text: A hypothesis not yet derived or tested (block Y), or a task not yet executed (block T).

legend.name: $\Om$-hard
legend.text: Decided by the totality; not closeable by a bounded observer; read from the chart.

C1.name: FRC.Hadrons.colour_group
C1.doc: 35:C1, 35:X2 — the colour group built exactly: `36` unit vectors, `648` orthonormal frames (`U(3, 2)`), `216` of determinant one (`SU(3, 2)`), every element unitary (`g†g = I`) with `det g = 1`; the triality centre: the elements commuting with `D1` and `U1` are exactly the three scalars `I, wI, w²I`, and each scalar commutes with the whole group. `su3_centre` of the interactions theme shows the scalars central; here the centre is no larger.

C1.name: FRC.Interactions.su3_centre
C1.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 35:C1, 35:X2 — the scalar centre of `SU(3, 2)` over `𝔽₄`: the scalars `x I` with `x x̄ = 1` and `x³ = 1` are the three cube roots of unity `1, w, w²` (`ℤ₃`, colour triality), `0` is not one, and each commutes with `U₁` and `U₂`; that the centre is no larger is 27-fields' ledger check E1 (all `216²` products) and, in the kernel, the hadrons theme's `FRC.Hadrons.colour_group` (the commutant of `D₁` and `U₁` in the group built by frames is the three scalars).

C2.name: FRC.Hadrons.gmo
C2.doc: 35:C2, 35:X4, 35:X13, 35:P1 — Gell-Mann–Okubo as a ring identity: `2N + 2Ξ − 3Λ − Σ = 0` for every `M₀, a, c`; the scale and the breaking parameters cancel.

C3.name: FRC.Hadrons.spacing
C3.doc: 35:C3, 35:X5, 35:X13, 35:P2 — decuplet equal spacing as a ring identity: the two second differences `Δ − 2Σ* + Ξ*` and `Σ* − 2Ξ* + Ω` vanish for every `α, β`.

C4.name: FRC.Hadrons.colour_factor
C4.doc: 35:C4, 35:X6 — the colour factor of the singlet with denominators cleared: `2N C₂(𝟛) = N² − 1` gives `6 C₂ = 8` (`C₂ = 4/3`); `2 Σ_{i<j} T_i·T_j = C₂(𝟙) − 3 C₂(𝟛)` gives `12 Σ T·T = −24` (`−2`); `λ = 2T` gives `Σ λ·λ = −8`, `−8/3` per pair.

C5.name: FRC.Hadrons.spin_pattern
C5.doc: 35:C5, 35:X6, 35:P3 — the spin pattern with denominators cleared: for `S = n/2`, `8 g_spin = 8[½S(S+1) − 9/8] = n(n+2) − 9`: the octet (`n = 1`) `−6/8 = −3/4`, the decuplet (`n = 3`) `6/8 = 3/4`, the separation `12/8 = 3/2`; the eigenvalues of `Σ(λ·λ)(S·S)` on the singlet, `(−8/3) g`: `(−8)(−6) = 48 = 2 · 24` (`+2`) and `(−8)(6) = −48` (`−2`).

C7.name: FRC.Hadrons.coleman_glashow
C7.doc: 35:C7, 35:X10, 35:X13, 35:P6 — Coleman–Glashow as a one-body identity: counting the `d − u` content, `n − p = δ`, `Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰ = δ`, `Σ⁻ − Σ⁺ = 2δ`, so `(n − p) + (Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰) − (Σ⁻ − Σ⁺) = 0` for every one-body unit `δ`.

C7.name: FRC.Hadrons.cg_charge_sums
C7.doc: 35:C7, 35:C13 — the charge sums of the six states of Coleman–Glashow with `9Q²` integral (`p = uud`, `n = udd`, `Ξ⁰ = uss`, `Ξ⁻ = dss`, `Σ⁺ = uus`, `Σ⁻ = dds`): the one-body sums `9 Σ Q²` are `9, 6, 6, 3, 9, 3` and the two-body sums `9 Σ_{i<j} Q_iQ_j` are `0, −3, −3, 3, 0, 3`; for each, `(n − p) + (Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰) = Σ⁻ − Σ⁺`.

C8.name: FRC.Hadrons.charge_structure
C8.doc: 35:C8, 35:C13, 35:C21, 35:X8 — the charge structure with `9Q²` integral (`Q_u = 2/3`, `Q_d = −1/3`): one-body `9 Σ Q² = 4 + 4 + 1 = 9` for the proton (`1`) and `4 + 1 + 1 = 6` for the neutron (`2/3`); two-body `9 Σ_{i<j} Q_iQ_j = 4 − 2 − 2 = 0` for the proton and `−2 − 2 + 1 = −3` for the neutron (`−1/3`); both differences `p − n` positive (`+3`, `+3`, that is `+1/3` each): the electromagnetic term makes the proton heavier.

C9.name: FRC.Hadrons.sigma_lambda
C9.doc: 35:C9, 35:X9 — the `Σ`–`Λ` fine structure: the light pair's `S_u·S_d` is `−3/4` at spin `0` and `+1/4` at spin `1` (`4 S·S = 2S(S+1) − 3`: `−3`, `+1`); the strange quark's coupling to the pair, `2 S_s·(S_u + S_d) = S(S+1) − S_ud(S_ud+1) − 3/4` at total spin `½` (`4S(S+1) = 3`): `0` for the spin-`0` pair, `−1` for the spin-`1` pair (`8 S_s·S_pair = 3 − 4S_ud(S_ud+1) − 3`: `0`, `−8`). So `M_Σ − M_Λ = a_ll(1/4 + 3/4) + a_ls(−1 − 0) = a_ll − a_ls`.

C10.name: FRC.Hadrons.hqs_identity
C10.doc: 35:C10, 35:X11, 35:P7 — the heavy-quark relation in the pairwise model: `M_{Λ_b} − M_{Λ_c} = m_b − m_c`, and the spin averages of the heavy mesons give the same difference, `(M_P + 3M_V)_B − (M_P + 3M_V)_D = 4(M_{Λ_b} − M_{Λ_c})`, for every value of the masses and of the hyperfine coefficients.

C11.name: FRC.Hadrons.third_difference
C11.doc: 35:C11 — the decuplet third difference vanishes identically in the model: `Δ − 3Σ* + 3Ξ* − Ω = 0` for every `M₀, d, A, r`.

C11.name: FRC.Hadrons.second_order
C11.doc: 35:C11, 35:C20 — the second order of the pairwise model, with `A = 4a` and `r = m_l/m_s`: both decuplet second differences `Δ − 2Σ* + Ξ*` and `Σ* − 2Ξ* + Ω` equal `a(1 − r)² = (A/4)(1 − r)²`, and `2N + 2Ξ − 3Λ − Σ = 2a(1 − r)²`, that is the octet residual `½(N + Ξ) − ¼(3Λ + Σ) = (A/8)(1 − r)²`; for every `M₀, d, A, r`.

C12.name: FRC.Hadrons.hyperfine_links
C12.doc: 35:C12 — the two octet–decuplet hyperfine links, parameter-free: `3(Σ − Λ) = 2[(Δ − N) − (Σ* − Σ)]` and `(Σ* − Σ) − (Ξ* − Ξ) = 0`.

C13.name: FRC.Hadrons.charge_structure
C13.doc: 35:C8, 35:C13, 35:C21, 35:X8 — the charge structure with `9Q²` integral (`Q_u = 2/3`, `Q_d = −1/3`): one-body `9 Σ Q² = 4 + 4 + 1 = 9` for the proton (`1`) and `4 + 1 + 1 = 6` for the neutron (`2/3`); two-body `9 Σ_{i<j} Q_iQ_j = 4 − 2 − 2 = 0` for the proton and `−2 − 2 + 1 = −3` for the neutron (`−1/3`); both differences `p − n` positive (`+3`, `+3`, that is `+1/3` each): the electromagnetic term makes the proton heavier.

C13.name: FRC.Hadrons.cg_charge_sums
C13.doc: 35:C7, 35:C13 — the charge sums of the six states of Coleman–Glashow with `9Q²` integral (`p = uud`, `n = udd`, `Ξ⁰ = uss`, `Ξ⁻ = dss`, `Σ⁺ = uus`, `Σ⁻ = dds`): the one-body sums `9 Σ Q²` are `9, 6, 6, 3, 9, 3` and the two-body sums `9 Σ_{i<j} Q_iQ_j` are `0, −3, −3, 3, 0, 3`; for each, `(n − p) + (Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰) = Σ⁻ − Σ⁺`.

C14.name: FRC.Hadrons.adjoint_channel
C14.doc: 35:C14 — the classical count of the adjoint channel, as moments of `SU(3)` by the Weyl constant term: `E[χχ̄] = 1` (`𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` has one singlet), `E[χ²] = 0` (`𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has none), `E[χ²χ̄²] − E[χχ̄] = 1` (the adjoint `𝟠 = χχ̄ − 1` sits in `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` once), `E[χ³χ̄] − E[χ²] = 0` (`𝟠` is absent from `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛`). The last two clauses are the integers `2·3² = 18` and `(2·3)² = 36`.

C15.name: FRC.Hadrons.colourless_content
C15.doc: 35:C15, 35:X1, 35:X3, 35:X7, 35:P4 — the colourless content of `Λ•(𝟛)` is `(1, 0, 0, 1)`: the vacuum; no nonzero vector of `𝟛` fixed by the group (a single quark has residue `0`); none of `Λ²(𝟛) ≅ 𝟛̄` (the diquark); `Λ³(𝟛) = det`, fixed by every element (`det g = 1`), the one-dimensional invariant — the baryon at `k = N = 3`, residue `1`. The dimensions `1, 3, 3, 1` sum to `8 = 2³`.

C15.name: FRC.Hadrons.no_invariant_line
C15.doc: 35:C15, 35:X1 — no line of the triplet `𝟛` and no line of `Λ²(𝟛) ≅ 𝟛̄` is mapped to itself by every element of `SU(3, 2)`: no nonzero vector `v` has `g v ∈ {v, w v, w² v}` for all `216` elements. A registration is a line that the frame maps to itself, so a single quark and a diquark have residue `0`.

C16.name: FRC.Hadrons.lambda_n_gap
C16.doc: 35:C16, 35:P10 — the Λ–N gap is the strange constituent excess: `M_Λ − M_N = m_s − m_l` for every `l, s, u`, the hyperfine cancelling.

C16.name: FRC.Hadrons.spin_split
C16.doc: 35:C16, 35:C19, 35:P10 — the exact spin split inverts: `M_N + M_Δ = 6λ_l` and `M_Δ − M_N = 6f = (3/2)λ_hf`, so `λ_l = (M_N + M_Δ)/6` and `λ_hf = (2/3)(M_Δ − M_N)`.

C17.name: FRC.Hadrons.airy_sturm
C17.doc: 35:C17 — the nonrelativistic matrix `H^{(N)} = −u'' + x u` on `N = 200` sites of `[0, 16]`: Sturm's count of the integer tridiagonal `201³ T + 16³ K` at `μ = 201 · 256 · ε` places exactly one eigenvalue in `(2.33, 2.34)`, one in `(4.08, 4.09)`, one in `(5.51, 5.52)` and one in `(6.77, 6.79)`: the spectrum sits at the decimals of the Airy zeros to the grid's accuracy (the readout `2.338, 4.088, 5.521, 6.787` is the chart's).

C18.name: FRC.Hadrons.meson_invariant
C18.doc: 35:C18, 35:X12 — the meson contraction: `g†g = I` for every element is the invariance of the Hermitian form on the basis pairs, `⟨g e_i, g e_j⟩ = (g†g)_{ij} = δ_{ij}`, so the `q q̄` contraction `v^a w̄_a` is the one-dimensional invariant of `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄`; the triality of `q q̄` is `1 + 2 ≡ 0`, of `qqq` is `3 ≡ 0` (mod 3).

C18.name: FRC.Hadrons.vector_spacing
C18.doc: 35:C18, 35:X12, 35:X13, 35:P9 — the vector-nonet equal spacing as a ring identity: `2K* − ρ − φ = 0` for every `a, b`.

C24.name: FRC.Hadrons.winding_register
C24.doc: 35:C24 — the winding law in the Carrier register, on the Carriers `233`, `30089` and `2408561`: `4c⁴ ≡ 1` and `h = −ħ` is the partner of `ħ` in the root pair of `−1`, so `4M²c⁴ ≡ N hcσ` reads `M² ≡ N hcσ`. On the Subjects `13`, `173` and `1549` the squares of the ratios are the residues `(4k + 3)κ`, with `4κ = p − 1` for each radial step.

C25.name: FRC.Hadrons.no_real_class
C25.doc: 35:C25 — on the Subjects `13`, `173` and `1549` with the drive `2`: the drive has the order `p − 1`, and no odd power of it below `p − 1` is `1` or `−1`, so no odd class of the drive is real; over `𝔽_q`, `q = 53, 347, 6197` the least prime `≡ 1 (mod p)` and `ζ = 16, 4, 16` of order `p`, the commutator of the register's Hamiltonian with the drive on the odd function `δ₁ − δ₋₁` reads `34`, `174`, `4364` at the residue `2`: it is not zero.

C26.name: FRC.Hadrons.scale_register
C26.doc: 35:C26 — the scale in the Carrier register, on the Carriers `233`, `30089` and `2408561`: for both roots `ħ` of `−1` and both roots `c` of `2⁻¹`, `(ħc)² ≡ −2⁻¹ ≡ 2S`, so the fourth power of the scale `√(ħcσ)` is `2S σ²`.

C27.name: FRC.Hadrons.winding_no_root
C27.doc: 35:C27 — no choice of the roots enters the winding law, on the Carriers `233`, `30089` and `2408561`: with `2G + 1 ≡ 0` the Planck mass squared `ħc/G` is `2hc` for both roots `ħ` of `−1` and both roots `c` of `2⁻¹`, so `M² ≡ N hcσ` reads `(M/m_P)² ≡ N σ/2` and `(Mc²)² ≡ N S · ħcσ`.

X13.doc: 35:C18, 35:X12, 35:X13, 35:P9 — the vector-nonet equal spacing as a ring identity: `2K* − ρ − φ = 0` for every `a, b`.

P1.name: FRC.Hadrons.gmo
P1.doc: 35:C2, 35:X4, 35:X13, 35:P1 — Gell-Mann–Okubo as a ring identity: `2N + 2Ξ − 3Λ − Σ = 0` for every `M₀, a, c`; the scale and the breaking parameters cancel.

P2.name: FRC.Hadrons.spacing
P2.doc: 35:C3, 35:X5, 35:X13, 35:P2 — decuplet equal spacing as a ring identity: the two second differences `Δ − 2Σ* + Ξ*` and `Σ* − 2Ξ* + Ω` vanish for every `α, β`.

P3.name: FRC.Hadrons.spin_pattern
P3.doc: 35:C5, 35:X6, 35:P3 — the spin pattern with denominators cleared: for `S = n/2`, `8 g_spin = 8[½S(S+1) − 9/8] = n(n+2) − 9`: the octet (`n = 1`) `−6/8 = −3/4`, the decuplet (`n = 3`) `6/8 = 3/4`, the separation `12/8 = 3/2`; the eigenvalues of `Σ(λ·λ)(S·S)` on the singlet, `(−8/3) g`: `(−8)(−6) = 48 = 2 · 24` (`+2`) and `(−8)(6) = −48` (`−2`).

P4.name: FRC.Hadrons.colourless_content
P4.doc: 35:C15, 35:X1, 35:X3, 35:X7, 35:P4 — the colourless content of `Λ•(𝟛)` is `(1, 0, 0, 1)`: the vacuum; no nonzero vector of `𝟛` fixed by the group (a single quark has residue `0`); none of `Λ²(𝟛) ≅ 𝟛̄` (the diquark); `Λ³(𝟛) = det`, fixed by every element (`det g = 1`), the one-dimensional invariant — the baryon at `k = N = 3`, residue `1`. The dimensions `1, 3, 3, 1` sum to `8 = 2³`.

P5.name: FRC.Hadrons.flavour_cube
P5.doc: 35:P5 — the flavour cube `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 = 𝟙𝟘 ⊕ 𝟠 ⊕ 𝟠 ⊕ 𝟙`: one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`), the adjoint twice (`E[χ⁴χ̄] − E[χ³] = 2`), the squared multiplicities summing to `E[χ³χ̄³] = 6 = 1 + 2² + 1`, the dimensions `27 = 10 + 8 + 8 + 1`; the symmetric spin–flavour cube `Sym³(𝟞)` has `8·7·6/3! = 56 = 10 · 4 + 8 · 2` states: no multiplet beyond the `𝟠` and the `𝟙𝟘` at leading order.

P6.name: FRC.Hadrons.coleman_glashow
P6.doc: 35:C7, 35:X10, 35:X13, 35:P6 — Coleman–Glashow as a one-body identity: counting the `d − u` content, `n − p = δ`, `Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰ = δ`, `Σ⁻ − Σ⁺ = 2δ`, so `(n − p) + (Ξ⁻ − Ξ⁰) − (Σ⁻ − Σ⁺) = 0` for every one-body unit `δ`.

P7.name: FRC.Hadrons.hqs_identity
P7.doc: 35:C10, 35:X11, 35:P7 — the heavy-quark relation in the pairwise model: `M_{Λ_b} − M_{Λ_c} = m_b − m_c`, and the spin averages of the heavy mesons give the same difference, `(M_P + 3M_V)_B − (M_P + 3M_V)_D = 4(M_{Λ_b} − M_{Λ_c})`, for every value of the masses and of the hyperfine coefficients.

P9.name: FRC.Hadrons.vector_spacing
P9.doc: 35:C18, 35:X12, 35:X13, 35:P9 — the vector-nonet equal spacing as a ring identity: `2K* − ρ − φ = 0` for every `a, b`.

P10.name: FRC.Hadrons.spin_split
P10.doc: 35:C16, 35:C19, 35:P10 — the exact spin split inverts: `M_N + M_Δ = 6λ_l` and `M_Δ − M_N = 6f = (3/2)λ_hf`, so `λ_l = (M_N + M_Δ)/6` and `λ_hf = (2/3)(M_Δ − M_N)`.

P10.name: FRC.Hadrons.lambda_n_gap
P10.doc: 35:C16, 35:P10 — the Λ–N gap is the strange constituent excess: `M_Λ − M_N = m_s − m_l` for every `l, s, u`, the hyperfine cancelling.
